evidence.observation: slugify() is the normalization primitive this contract is built on. It scans the title character by character, flushing alternating CJK and latin/alnum tokens, lowercasing only latin tokens, treating every space/punctuation character as a segment boundary, then joins with '-' and strips duplicate/edge hyphens. Because it is a pure string->string function with no state and no I/O, the same title always yields the same slug: 'Aloe Vera' and 'aloe  vera!' both normalize to 'aloe-vera'. That identity is what makes duplicate entities detectable, and it is what the demo proves by re-running normalization under shuffled input order and re-hashing the result.

dirForType() maps a page type to its wiki directory via the TYPE_DIR table (slug.ts:72-81), trimming and lowercasing the key and falling back to the raw key (or 'other' when empty) for unknown types. This is the second half of path normalization: it decides that a malformed or missing `type` lands in the generic 'other' directory rather than throwing. In the demo corpus, documents whose `type` is blank, numeric, or unparsed all normalize into wiki/other/*, deterministically and explicitly.

pageRelPath(type, title) composes slugify(title) with dirForType(type) into 'wiki/<dir>/<slug>.md'. It is the dedup gateway: a second ingest of the same entity name produces the identical relative path, so the writer finds the existing page and merges (merge.ts:70-109) instead of creating a second file. The demo asserts this is a pure function by calling it twice per document and comparing, and shows two differently-spelled documents collapsing onto the single path wiki/entities/aloe-vera.md.

CJK_RE plus the isCjkChar/isAlnumChar predicates classify each character, and they are the reason normalization is lossless for non-ASCII: CJK ideographs are retained verbatim (never romanized, never dropped) while only latin runs are lowercased and punctuation is treated as a boundary. This keeps slugs stable for mixed-language titles such as 'Redis 主从 Cluster' -> 'redis-主从-cluster', which is why the demo's idempotence check (slugify(slug) === slug) holds for every emitted anchor.

parseFrontmatter() is the tolerant frontmatter contract: it matches FM_RE (frontmatter.ts:36), and on any failure -- no fence, YAML parse error, or a non-object result -- returns `{type:'other'}` with the remainder as body and hasFrontmatter:false, never throwing. Line 60 additionally folds a missing/blank/non-string `type` down to 'other'. The demo mirrors this observable behaviour exactly and adds typed diagnostics for each branch, so the downgrade is explicit instead of silent.

readSources() accepts only arrays of strings and returns [] for anything else -- a scalar `sources:` value is discarded rather than coerced into a one-element list. The demo's SOURCES_NOT_ARRAY diagnostic fires on exactly this case (corpus files 02 and 05) and records that the value was dropped instead of guessed, keeping the raw/rm cascade contract sound.

isLocked() uses a strict `frontmatter.locked === true` test, so the string "true" does NOT lock a page. This is the contract's sharpest invalid-metadata case: guessing that an unparseable lock flag means 'locked' would silently protect a page the user never locked, so the tolerant path degrades to unlocked and the demo emits LOCKED_NOT_BOOLEAN to say so out loud.

unionSources() merges two source lists into a de-duplicated union, skipping non-strings and blanks and preserving first-seen order. It is the deterministic result of a dedup hit: when the demo's two 'Aloe Vera' spelling variants land on one page path, the normalized entity carries the union of both documents' sources rather than one document overwriting the other.

mergePage() defines what a duplicate slug means. A null existing content writes a new page; an existing locked page is skipped (never overwritten); otherwise the page is merged, with a rule-based redundancy short-circuit (merge.ts:55-60) ahead of the LLM paths. It is the contract that makes 'duplicate heading / duplicate entity' a merge decision rather than a file-name race, and it is why the demo reports mergedDocuments per normalized page rather than reporting a collision error.

splitIntoUnits() splits a document at markdown heading boundaries using `isHeading = /^#{1,6}\s+\S/` (chunker.ts:32). The demo's section scanner mirrors that same heading pattern, which is what makes 'duplicate headings' a real case rather than a synthetic one: repeated heading text produces repeated section units, and the demo assigns them stable ordinal anchors (overview, overview-2, ...) instead of letting the second one shadow the first.

claims.claim: Normalization is deterministic: slugify() and pageRelPath() are pure functions, so a corpus normalized twice, or normalized under a shuffled document order, yields a byte-identical canonical result. The demo builds the report five times (two file-order runs plus three seeded shuffles) and all five canonical SHA-256 digests are 5274fe8f4ef02ae92621d030e637e6a8189e8e278c269da77049651521d3f12e.

Duplicate headings are handled deterministically: repeated heading text within one document is normalized to ordinal-suffixed section anchors (overview, overview-2, succulent-overview-2, grafting-2), so no occurrence is shadowed; every anchor is a fixed point of slugify. The demo asserts this over 18 anchors across the 7-document corpus.

Duplicate entities across documents are merged, not duplicated: 'Aloe Vera' and 'aloe  vera!' normalize to the same slug and therefore the same page path wiki/entities/aloe-vera.md, collapsing two corpus documents onto one normalized page with a de-duplicated union of sources.

Malformed frontmatter is handled explicitly rather than silently: an absent frontmatter block, an unterminated fence, a YAML parse failure, a blank or non-string `type`, a scalar `sources`, and a non-boolean `locked` each downgrade to the documented tolerant outcome AND emit a typed diagnostic. The demo asserts that all ten expected diagnostic codes (NO_FRONTMATTER, UNTERMINATED_FRONTMATTER, YAML_PARSE_ERROR, TYPE_ABSENT, TYPE_EMPTY, TYPE_NOT_STRING, SOURCES_NOT_ARRAY, LOCKED_NOT_BOOLEAN, TITLE_MISSING, DUPLICATE_HEADING) actually fire on the corpus; 19 diagnostics were emitted in total.

The `locked` flag is resolved strictly: the string "true" does not lock a page, so an unparseable lock flag degrades to unlocked and is reported (LOCKED_NOT_BOOLEAN) rather than guessed into protecting a page the user never locked.

conclusion: Contracting a different corpus (seven succulent-care notes carrying duplicate headings and six distinct classes of malformed metadata) against the repository's normalization module shows the transferable contract holds: slugify/dirForType/pageRelPath are pure, idempotent mappings, so normalization is deterministic (five runs, file order and three seeded shuffles, all produce canonical sha256 5274fe8f4ef02ae92621d030e637e6a8189e8e278c269da77049651521d3f12e) and duplicate headings resolve to stable ordinal anchors while duplicate entities collapse onto one merged page path. Invalid metadata is never silently absorbed: each defect downgrades to the tolerant outcome documented in frontmatter.ts (type -> "other", sources -> [], locked -> unlocked, title derived from the first heading) and simultaneously emits a typed diagnostic, with all ten expected codes firing. The executable demo `.prale-eval/normalize-corpus.ts` exits 0 only when determinism, order-independence, idempotence, the duplicate-heading exercise, the cross-document merge, and full diagnostic coverage all hold.

validation.notes: Exit code 0. The demo imports the real MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/ingest-v2/slug.ts verbatim (Node 24 native type-stripping; that module has no third-party imports) and self-asserts five properties: repeat-run hash match, order-independence across three seeded shuffles, idempotence of every slug/page path/section anchor, that duplicate headings and a cross-document duplicate entity both occur, and that all ten expected diagnostic codes fire. Result: 7 documents -> 6 normalized pages, 19 diagnostics, canonical sha256 5274fe8f4ef02ae92621d030e637e6a8189e8e278c269da77049651521d3f12e identical across 5 runs; report written to .prale-eval/normalized-report.json. LIMITATION: the repository's own frontmatter.ts depends on the `yaml` package, and no node_modules are present in this checkout; dependencies must not be installed, so frontmatter.ts (and therefore vitest, whose `npm test` script is defined in MemoryKnowledge/package.json but has no installed runner) was NOT executed. The tolerant frontmatter contract is re-implemented in the demo over a documented minimal YAML subset that reproduces the observable behaviour of frontmatter.ts:42-76 (FM_RE fence split, parse-failure downgrade, non-empty-string type fallback, sources array requirement, strict locked === true). The module named by the acceptance contract, slug.ts, is executed directly and unmodified.
